record.paper_title: The Interiors of Uranus and Neptune: Current Understanding and Open Questions
record.original_question: How large is the family of interior density structures allowed by the current gravity fields of Uranus and Neptune, including the poorly sampled innermost 30 percent of each planet and the lack of useful sixth-degree gravitational-harmonic constraints?

evidence.quote: Given that a wide range of structures are possible to fit the gravity fields of each planet, this naturally begs the question regarding how large the possible range of solutions really is?

For both Uranus and Neptune the innermost 30% of the planets is not well sampled by the gravitational harmonics. As a result, conclusions about the innermost part of the planets must be inferred indirectly.
In addition, the error bar on J6 on either planet is so large that it provides no real additional constraint.

artifact.category_tag: inverse problems for planetary gravity fields
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a rotating, fluid, axially symmetric planet in hydrostatic equilibrium occupying the ball of radius R. Its interior mass distribution is described by a density field ρ(r, μ), where r ∈ [0, R] is the radial coordinate and μ = cos θ is the cosine of the colatitude. The exterior gravitational potential, evaluated outside the planet, admits the multipole expansion

U(r, μ) = (GM/r) [ 1 − Σ_{n≥1} (R/r)^{2n} J_{2n} P_{2n}(μ) ],

where P_{2n} are Legendre polynomials and J_{2n} are the (even) zonal gravitational harmonic coefficients defined by

J_{2n} = − (1/(M R^{2n})) ∫_planet ρ(r', μ') (r')^{2n} P_{2n}(μ') dV'.

Fix the planetary mass M, equatorial radius R, and uniform rotation rate Ω, and suppose ρ is required to be non-negative, monotonically non-increasing in r along each colatitude, and consistent with hydrostatic balance under self-gravity and centrifugal forcing for some barotropic equation of state.

Let J_2^obs and J_4^obs be specified with prescribed observational uncertainty intervals [J_2^obs ± σ_2] and [J_4^obs ± σ_4], while J_6 is treated as essentially unconstrained (its uncertainty interval covering the full physically plausible range). Assume in addition that the radial region 0 ≤ r ≤ 0.3 R contributes negligibly to J_2 and J_4 within their uncertainties, so that the density there is effectively unconstrained by J_2 and J_4.

Problem. Characterise the set

𝒮 = { ρ(r, μ) : ρ satisfies the structural and hydrostatic constraints above, and the J_{2n}[ρ] computed from ρ lie within the prescribed observational intervals for n = 1, 2, with no constraint imposed for n ≥ 3 },

and, in particular, quantify the size (e.g. the range of admissible inner-core masses, central densities, mean molecular-weight profiles, and bulk compositional gradients) of 𝒮 for the rotation rate, mass and radius parameters of Uranus and of Neptune. Equivalently, provide sharp bounds, or a complete parametric description, of all interior density profiles ρ(r, μ) compatible with the present-day measured gravitational harmonics of these two planets.
artifact.status_search_result: The degeneracy of interior-structure models for Uranus and Neptune given current gravity-field data is widely acknowledged as an open problem in planetary science. Recent reviews and modeling studies emphasize that many distinct density profiles fit the available J_2, J_4 within uncertainties, that the inner ~30% of each planet is essentially unconstrained, and that improved constraints (notably J_6 and higher harmonics, achievable only through future orbiter missions such as a proposed Uranus Probe/Orbiter) are required to reduce this degeneracy. No definitive characterisation of the admissible family has been established.

status_evidence.title: The Interiors of Uranus and Neptune: Current Understanding and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: A wide range of interior structures fit the gravity fields; the innermost 30% is poorly sampled and J6 errors are too large to constrain models.
status_evidence.claim: Interior density profiles of Uranus and Neptune compatible with current gravity data form a large, poorly characterised family.

status_evidence.title: Uranus Orbiter and Probe – Planetary Decadal Survey 2023
status_evidence.snippet: A Uranus orbiter is recommended in part to obtain higher-order gravity harmonics needed to break interior-structure degeneracies.
status_evidence.claim: Resolving the interior-structure degeneracy is identified as an outstanding open problem requiring future missions.
